content.title: Management of right ventricular failure / 11.2.4 Cardiogenic shock
content.figure_caption: Management of right ventricular failure. Notes: ACS = acute coronary syndrome; RV = right ventricular; RVAD = right ventricular assist device. a Inotropes alone in case of hypoperfusion without hypotension.
flowchart_summary: Assess for ACS with RV involvement or acute pulmonary embolism; if present, give specific treatments.
Optimize fluid status; if marked congestion, give loop diuretics (Class I).
If peripheral hypoperfusion/persistent hypotension present, consider vasopressors and/or inotropes (Class IIb).
If no relief of signs/symptoms: consider RVAD and/or renal replacement therapy or consider palliative care.
content.definition: Cardiogenic shock is a syndrome due to primary cardiac dysfunction resulting in inadequate cardiac output and tissue hypoperfusion, potentially causing multi-organ failure and death.
causes: Acute loss of myocardial tissue (acute MI, myocarditis)
Progressive decline in chronic decompensated heart failure (advanced HF or specific precipitants)
diagnosis_criteria: Clinical signs of hypoperfusion (cold, sweated extremities; oliguria; mental confusion; dizziness; narrow pulse pressure)
management_principles: Identify and treat underlying cause (e.g., ACS with RV involvement, PE)
Optimize volume status and congestion management (loop diuretics when congested)
Use vasopressors and/or inotropes in persistent hypotension/hypoperfusion
Escalate to mechanical circulatory support (e.g., RVAD) and/or renal replacement therapy if refractory
